candidates.teaser: Mercury retrograde ends in 7 days — but the last week is always the most dangerous.
candidates.video_title: Mercury Retrograde's Final Week Is the Worst One
candidates.video_description: Mercury stations direct on November 14 — but astrologers warn the final stretch of a retrograde cycle is where the real chaos peaks. Here's what to watch before the storm clears.
candidates.script: The last seven days of Mercury retrograde are always the most chaotic — and we're inside them right now. Mercury sits at 8° Scorpio, still reversed, and doesn't station direct until November 14. In traditional astrology, the final stretch before a station is called the storm window — this is when miscommunications peak, contracts backfire, and buried truths surface without warning. Scorpio doesn't soften any of that. What conversation have you been avoiding?

candidates.topic: New Moon in Libra — Five Retrogrades Backdrop
candidates.teaser: A New Moon just landed in Libra — but five planets are still retrograde. Can you actually start fresh right now?
candidates.video_title: New Moon in Libra — Can You Start Fresh With 5 Retrogrades?
candidates.video_description: Today's New Moon falls at 25° Libra — normally a signal for new beginnings. But with Mercury, Venus, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune all retrograde simultaneously, astrologers say this lunation asks for reflection over action.
candidates.script: There's a New Moon in Libra right now — and normally that means fresh starts, new relationships, clean slates. But five planets are retrograde at this exact moment: Mercury, Venus, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Astrologers call this kind of lunation a sealed moon — the energy turns inward instead of launching outward. At 25° Libra, the Moon sits close to Venus retrograde at 23°. This isn't a beginning. It's a reckoning. What needs balancing before you can actually move forward?

candidates.topic: Venus Retrograde in Libra — Conjunct New Moon
candidates.teaser: Venus is retrograde in its own sign — and today's New Moon is sitting right next to it. This is rare.
candidates.video_title: Venus Retrograde Conjunct the New Moon — What This Means
candidates.video_description: Venus retrograde at 23° Libra is within two degrees of today's New Moon at 25° Libra. In astrology, a Venus-Moon conjunction during a retrograde cycle intensifies questions around self-worth, relationships, and what we genuinely value.
candidates.script: Venus is retrograde in Libra — its own sign — and today's New Moon just landed two degrees away from it. That's not a coincidence you ignore. In astrology, when the Moon meets a retrograde Venus during a new lunar cycle, the theme isn't attraction — it's re-evaluation. Libra rules partnerships, fairness, and what you're willing to compromise. Venus retrograde strips that down. The question this sky is asking you: are you staying in something out of love, or out of habit?

candidates.topic: Rising Sign vs Sun Sign — The Difference
candidates.teaser: Your Sun sign is just your costume. Your rising sign is your whole first impression — and most people have it wrong.
candidates.video_title: Your Rising Sign Matters More Than Your Sun Sign
candidates.video_description: In modern astrology, the rising sign — or Ascendant — governs how the world sees you, the structure of your birth chart, and which house system your life runs on. Many astrologers argue it's more personally telling than your Sun sign.
candidates.script: Your Sun sign describes your core identity — but your rising sign is what every single person sees before you even speak. In astrology, the Ascendant is calculated from your exact birth time and location, and it shifts every two hours. It rules the mask you wear, the body you move through the world in, and the entire architecture of your birth chart. Two people born the same day can have completely different charts because of it. Do you know your rising sign — and does it fit better than your Sun?

candidates.topic: Saturn Conjunct Neptune in Aries — Rare Alignment
candidates.teaser: Saturn and Neptune are both retrograde in Aries right now — and they're less than 7 degrees apart. The last time this happened was decades ago.
candidates.video_title: Saturn and Neptune Both Retrograde in Aries — Rare
candidates.video_description: With Saturn at 8° Aries and Neptune at 2° Aries, both retrograde simultaneously, astrologers describe a collision between structure and dissolution. This pairing in Aries — the sign of beginnings — creates a rare tension between building something and questioning whether it should exist at all.
candidates.script: Saturn sits at 8° Aries retrograde. Neptune sits at 2° Aries retrograde. They are closing in on each other — and in astrology, this is one of the rarest and most disorienting conjunctions in the sky. Saturn builds walls. Neptune dissolves them. When both reverse through Aries — the sign of raw, forward-driving identity — traditional astrologers say entire structures people believed in begin to feel uncertain. Systems, beliefs, even self-image. What have you built that you're no longer sure was real?
